propositions: The outbound differ compares in vendor shape while the inbound differ compares in canonical shape, creating an asymmetry that violates the port abstraction boundary and blocks epic bbf1 AC3.

The outbound update path reads raw Jira snapshot keys (fields.status.name, assignee.accountId, parent.key, description ADF) directly in core, forcing vendors onto the Backend port and violating ADR 0035 §(d).
The snapshot must be canonicalized via InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local before any field comparison, and vendor payloads must be emitted only via OutboundMapper.map_fields_to_remote at the boundary.

InboundMapper output must include three new canonical alias keys (assignee_identity, remote_parent_id, reporter_identity) that exist only when their source vendor keys are present, making map_remote_to_local tolerant of partial _BASELINE_FIELDS subsets.

The assignee resolver and _assignee_is_account_id sentinel must move to OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee, parameterized only on canonical assignee_identity shape, preserving the 3-state contract for the accountId fast-path and unmappable→unassign soft-fail.

Outbound field-comparison logic (issuetype exclusion, inbound-directionality suppression, ADF description fit+rstrip, label identity exclusion, conflict detection via canonicalized baseline) must be expressed in local field vocabulary with no vendor snapshot key literals in core modules.
